blocks.title: Michigan tint law: what to know before you book.
blocks.intro: Michigan's tint rules are different from most other states. We walk you through the details for your exact vehicle during your consultation. This is general information, not legal advice.

items.q: Is window tint legal in Michigan?
items.a:
Michigan allows window tint, but the rules on where film can go and how dark it can be are specific to each set of windows, and they are different from most other states.

During your consultation we walk you through what is legal for your exact vehicle, so you know where you stand before you choose a shade.

items.q: What about darker rear windows or a medical exemption?
items.a: Both are part of the consultation. We go over your options for darker rear windows on your vehicle. If you have a light-sensitive condition, we also walk you through Michigan's medical exemption process.

items.q: Who decides how dark my tint goes?
items.a:
You do. We show you the shades on real glass, tell you what is legal for your vehicle and help you land on a setup that looks right. The final shade choice is always yours, and so is the responsibility for picking a shade that complies with state and local law.

Tint laws can change and local enforcement varies, so we review current Michigan requirements with you during your consultation.

faq.q: How much does window tint cost?
faq.a:
On a standard coupe or sedan, C2 Carbon is from $99.99 for the front 2 windows, from $199.99 for full sides and from $299.99 for full sides + rear glass. C2 Ceramic is from $149.99, from $299.99 and from $399.99 for the same windows. A front windshield is from $175.00 and is done in ceramic film only.

SUVs and trucks are quoted by vehicle, and any adjustment is approved before work begins. [Request a free quote](#quote) for your exact price.

faq.q: What is the difference between carbon and ceramic tint?
faq.a:
Both are Geoshield C2 films, both are non-metalized, both block 99% of UV and both carry the lifetime warranty. The difference is heat: C2 Ceramic blocks far more infrared heat, so the cabin is noticeably cooler on a sunny day.

C2 Carbon is the pick for drivers focused on style and value. C2 Ceramic is the pick for drivers who want privacy, comfort and performance, and it costs more: the front 2 windows on a standard coupe or sedan are from $99.99 in carbon and from $149.99 in ceramic. Tell us how you drive and we will tell you straight which one fits.

faq.q: How long does window tint installation take?
faq.a:
Most installs are done the same day you drop off. The front 2 windows take about 1.5 hours, full sides about 2.5 hours, and full sides + rear glass about 3.5 hours. A front windshield is about 1.5 hours.

We are appointment only, so book your drop-off before you come by.

faq.q: When can I roll my windows down after tinting?
faq.a:
Give it 3 to 4 days before rolling tinted windows down, so the film fully bonds to the glass. You may notice small water pockets or a light haze during the first week. That is normal and clears on its own as the film cures.

Rolling the windows down too early is the one thing that can peel a fresh edge, so set a reminder and leave them up.

faq.q: Will my tint bubble or turn purple over time?
faq.a:
Low-grade dyed film does. That purple, bubbling look is the dye breaking down, and we do not install it. Our Geoshield C2 Carbon and C2 Ceramic films are color-stable and backed by a lifetime warranty covering bubbling, peeling and fading.

Combined with plotter cut patterns and an indoor install, the tint on your glass should outlast your ownership of the vehicle.

faq.q: Can you remove my old tint?
faq.a:
Yes. Old, purple or bubbling tint is stripped using controlled heat and adhesive removal that protects your rear defroster lines. Then the glass is cleaned to a factory-fresh finish, ready for new film.

Removal is from $50 per area, and it is 50% off when we install a full-vehicle tint the same day.

faq.q: Will window tint interfere with my phone, GPS or radio?
faq.a: No. C2 Carbon and C2 Ceramic are both non-metalized films, so neither one interferes with GPS, radio or phone signal.

faq.q: Do you tint at my home or workplace?
faq.a:
No. Window tint is shop only. Film needs a clean, controlled space to bond, and the wind, dust and pollen in a driveway or parking lot are what cause peeling and bubbling. Every install happens indoors at our shop at 33115 Louise Ave in Clinton Township.

If getting here is the hard part, ask about our [pick-up and drop-off valet](/mobile-detailing/): we pick the vehicle up, tint it at the shop and bring it back. Valet reaches about 30 to 40 minutes from Clinton Township.
